paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Jordan J.G. Wright Candidate's Full Name Jordan J.G. Wright Candidate's Pronouns he/him Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQ community? If so, please specify as you are comfortable* Not currently Office New York State Assembly District Number 70 Full Name of Campaign Committee(s) Wright For NY Campaign Website Wright4Harlem.com Campaign Social Media Handles https://www.facebook.com/Wright4Harlem https://www.instagram.com/JordanWright4Harlem https://x.com/Wright4Harlem If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. Absolutely! I’ve been proud to tout my previous Stonewall endorsement and hope to have it again! What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? As a lifelong Harlemite with a background in advocacy-Community Board member, COS to Yusef Salaam, Assemblyman-I am committed to addressing today’s challenges, including human rights, criminal justice reform, affordable housing & public safety. Being born, raised & reared in & by Harlem has granted me an invaluable perspective & understanding of the nuanced needs of the district. I'm a next generation leader committed to ensuring that everyone in our community has opportunities for success. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 1

[PDF page 2] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Since being elected to office, I have helped move and pass legislation that positively impacts the lives of LGBTQ individuals, including the Trans Wellness & Equity Fund. Harlem became the center of Black America because it was an oasis in a country drenched in prejudice. Black people found safety, community, inspiration and influence in a neighborhood where they were supported by plurality — many of the leaders at that time were queer. It is my duty, honor and moral imperative- as this region’s representative- to staunchly support the rights, safety, health and dignity of LGBTQ people, including Harlem’s own vibrant queer community. I have helped secure essential funding for non-profits in the district and statewide that provide invaluable services that many in the LGBTQ community utilize- from healthcare services to legal representation and street outreach- these community organizations offer an essential access point for LGBTQ folks who may be deterred from seeking traditional resources. I’ve marched in the NYC and Harlem Pride Parades since I was a little boy and was humbled to be awarded the NAACP Mid-Manhattan Branch - LGBTQ Ally Award in 2023. I led the successful campaign of a Stonewall Democratic Club-endorsed candidate- Councilmember Yusef Salaam. When I became his Chief of Staff, I made sure to include LGBTQ stakeholders in all discussions with community relevance; not only was this the right thing to do, it made for better, more robust policy and community work. But there is always more to be done, and I look forward to building on the momentum of my first term in office with Stonewall Dems and like-minded LGBTQ-led organizations helping guide the policy and programming priorities of the office of the 70th AD. What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? To be an effective representative for a community as diverse and vital as Harlem, USA is to be an effective representative for the LGBTQ community. Housing, job development and access, and youth services are three policy areas that I plan to continue to focus on in my second term. With LGBTQ individuals facing homelessness at an unsettlingly disproportionate rate, my fight for more affordable housing and tenant protections will help ensure that more folks have accessible homes. As I fight for augmented youth services and education, I will ensure that LGBTQ-specific opportunities are offered so that we can chip away at the gross discrimination faced by the community. I will use the full power of my office to ensure that LGBTQ voices are heard loud and clear. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. I am proud to have a number of endorsements we're rolling out in due time and I've been honored to have received Stonewall's endorsement in the past, as well as the support of Harlem Pride. Currently I have the public support of the following: Senator Cordell Cleare; Councilman Yusef Salaam; Hon. C. Virginia Fields; Comptroller Mark Levine; Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal; Hon. Ruben Diaz; Hon. Keith L.T. Wright; Hon. Inez Dickens; Assemblymember Catalina Cruz; District Leader Wilma Brown-Phillips; State Committee Member Alyah Horsford-Sidberry; State Committee Member Larry Scott Blackmon; 32 BJ; Columbia University Democrats; FDNYC: Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 2

[PDF page 3] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Uniformed Firefighters Association; FDNY Local 2507: Uniformed EMT, Paramedics and Inspectors Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ candidates? Which ones? Yes: Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal; Hon. Tony Simone; Senator Erik Bottcher Would you in the future endorse, appoint or financially support any candidate for public office, elected official, or political appointee with a record of opposing LGBTQ equality? If yes, please explain. * No Across the nation, and in New York State, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ legislation, including restricting the rights of trans youth, bans on LGBTQ books in schools, limits on drag queen performances, and limits on gender affirming care for minors and adults. How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for the protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state, and country? Across the nation, and in New York State, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ legislation, including restricting the rights of trans youth, bans on LGBTQ books in schools, limits on drag queen performances, and limits on gender affirming care for minors and adults. How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for the protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state, and country? * While New York may be considered, policy-wise, to be a safe haven for the LGBTQ community, as a legislator I will remain innovative, active and vigilant about protecting this population. Maintaining and strengthening free speech and expression in New York State is of the utmost importance, and being an outspoken advocate for LGBTQ rights is one way that I will continue to advocate for the protections of LGBTQ people across the city, state and country. It is high time to add LGBTQ-Inclusive Curricular Standards in New York State schools. My father implemented a piece of legislation that created a commission within the State Education Department that researches and ensures that the African slave trade, American slavery, and the contributions of African Americans are effectively taught in New York schools. I believe we can implement a similar mandate requiring education on the history and endurance of the LGBTQ population. It would be an excellent way to teach about organizing, overcoming, public health and public policy. If history repeats itself, we have a tremendous amount to learn about the struggles of LGBTQ folks in New York and beyond to avoid future mistakes that leads to discrimination, oppression and death. Our future generations deserve a relevant and well-rounded public education and there is tremendous value in learning about the uphill battle and continued work of the LGBTQ community. I will also continue to support and vote to approve increased funding for direct-service organizations who do the daily work of keeping the community — particularly LGBTQ youth and elderly — safe, healthy, and housed. The LGBTQ community has historically been overpoliced, and research shows that law enforcement continues to disproportionately target marginalized people: What do you view as the New York State Legislature's role in ensuring law enforcement oversight, funding, and role in meeting the needs of marginalized communities? What, if any, relevant policy proposals do you support regarding law enforcement? I am a leading advocate for police and criminal justice reform. The over-policing of LGBTQ people is steeped in systemic prejudice and is the opposite of effective policing. Marginalized groups, including the LGBTQ community and people of color, have continued to face over-policing.I believe that the foremost solutions revolve around transparency, Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 3

[PDF page 4] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires relationships, and accountability. As Chief of Staff to Councilman Yusef Salaam, I stood behind the How Many Stops Act, whose sole aim was to increase data collection around substantive police interactions. In my role as Assemblyman, I will continue to advocate for more community-based policing so that communities can truly get to know the officers tasked with keeping them safe. The fundamentals to public safety are also what’s fundamental to my campaign: housing, jobs & youth services. We must commit to addressing those issues if we ever expect to truly achieve public safety. In the People’s House, I have just introduced game-changing criminal justice legislation. It will begin a new era of race-blind criminal charging by using unbiased data to redact any information that could indicate race at the point of arrest. This means that from the first piece of paperwork to the documents given to prosecutors who make the decision whether to proceed with criminal charges, any information that could lead a reader to assume race would be redacted This includes skin color, names of witnesses and suspects, addresses and locations. So an individual stopped by police found to be in possession of cocaine while driving down Hollywood boulevard would prompt paperwork that looks nearly identical to the arrest log of someone on Malcolm X Boulevard accused of carrying crack cocaine. It’s how it should be and how it always should have been. A crime is a crime and the unneeded details that have led police and prosecutors to let internal biases dictate more harsh- or lenient- penalties have kept our prisons stacked with Black and Brown folks for decades. It’s a matter of fairness and by redacting these items from the jump, we help keep individuals from processing and entering the system that will follow them indefinitely, keeping them from accessing the jobs, housing and life that everyone deserves. What a beat cop surmised from someone’s name or appearance should not be a reason for any individual to struggle with the realities and discrimination of the criminal justice system. I believe this legislation will help protect black and brown LGBTQ individuals and the larger LGBTQ population. New York State is experiencing a housing crisis, and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do you intend to ensure that any housing plan is equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? I will continue to support housing initiatives that are inclusive and recognize the particularly vulnerable situation that LGBTQ youth and seniors face. The realities of today’s housing crisis grip our communities, it is imperative that we as legislators and decision makers understand the specific housing concerns of LGBTQ individuals. In the Assembly, I don’t fight for more housing for some, but for all. Without protections and guarantees for marginalized people, more housing does not translate to more housing for all. As a result, I will make sure to advocate for affordable units that are targeted at families, children and formerly homeless individuals and make sure that outreach from my office affirmatively strives to include our LGBTQ neighbors. In today’s political climate, what role should the New York Legislature play in protecting and expanding access to comprehensive reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare? Will you commit to defending access to abortion care and gender-affirming care for both adults and youth, including taking legislative action to prevent hospitals and healthcare systems—such as NYU Langone Health—from restricting or ending lifesaving care due to political pressure or federal intimidation? * Yes, I will commit to defending these essential healthcare services. [PDF page 5] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Privacy Amendment S8603 (Ramos) / A9377 (Shimsky) This amendment would enshrine a fundamental right to privacy in the New York Constitution, protecting personal decisions, bodily autonomy, and limiting government surveillance beyond federal standards. It is especially critical for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers whose sensitive data could otherwise be misused or weaponized. Yes Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE) S6901A (Salazar) / A7496 (Gonzalez-Rojas) This bill ensures age-appropriate, inclusive sex education statewide that reflects national standards. It reduces stigma, affirms LGBTQ+ students, and promotes safer, more informed school environments. Yes New York for All Act S2235 (Gounardes) / A3506 (Reyes) This bill limits state and local involvement in immigration enforcement, protecting immigrant families and public safety. It is vital for safeguarding LGBTQ+ immigrants who face heightened risks of targeting and discrimination. Yes Holding Police Accountable by Strengthening the Civilian Complaint Review Board S4354 (Bailey) / A126 (Cruz) This act expands the CCRB’s authority to investigate bias-based policing, which disproportionately harms LGBTQ+ people, particularly LGBTQ+ New Yorkers of color. It is a necessary step toward real accountability and trust in law enforcement. Yes The Gender Identity Respect Dignity and Safety Act (GIRDS) (A5478A - Gallagher/ S1049A Salazar) This bill ensures incarcerated transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals are treated with dignity, respected in placement, and provided gender-affirming necessities. It significantly improves safety and reduces abuse in correctional settings. Yes A6059 (Simone) / S03227 (Hoylman - Sigal) Prohibits health insurers, health care plans and HMOs from requiring prior authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis used to prevent HIV infection Yes The Freedom to Read Act S8630 (May) / A9537 (Simone) This bill prevents book bans based on LGBTQ+ identity or family structure in schools and libraries. It protects intellectual freedom and ensures young people can access accurate, inclusive representations of themselves and others. Yes A03251-A (Forrest) / S02513 (Salazar) Enacts "Cecilia's act for rights in the sex trades"; Decriminalizes certain prostitution offenses; amends provisions relating to prosecution of such offenses and vacating judgments. Yes A733 (Gonzalez-Rojas) Repeals criminal liability for persons living with sexually transmitted infections who engage in sexual activity.
